title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
authors: Jiří Adam, Andrei Alexandru, Navdeep Singh Dhindsa, Ivan Horváth, Frank X. Lee, Nilmani Mathur
abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power $p$ close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength $W$ of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power $p_1$ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with $p<0$ on an interval around $E = 1$ spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E = \infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E)=-1$ for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength $W$ rather than the lattice size $L$.
summary: This paper connects the theoretical prediction of a scale-invariant Dirac spectrum in the IR phase of QCD to a solvable condensed matter model: the chiral-orthogonal Anderson model. By analyzing the DOS under increasing disorder strength, the authors show that the model naturally evolves towards a universal power-law exponent of $-1$ in the infinite disorder limit. This suggests that the randomness strength $W$, rather than the lattice size $L$, dictates the relevant IR cutoff for modeling QCD phenomena.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the negative power-law density of states (DOS) near zero energy, characteristic of the Infrared (IR) phase of QCD, can be reproduced by chiral-orthogonal Anderson models.
main_result: The models do not exhibit a power-singular DOS at zero energy for finite disorder, but in the limit of infinite disorder strength, the DOS approaches a universal power law $ho(E) \propto E^{-1}$, mimicking the QCD prediction.
method: The authors analyze the spectrum of 3-D chiral-orthogonal Anderson models with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder, using numerical diagonalization and finite-size scaling to extrapolate the behavior in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The system is a 3-D chiral-orthogonal Anderson model defined on a lattice with periodic boundary conditions. The disorder is introduced via logarithmic off-diagonal hopping strengths $t$, which are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regulated by the disorder strength $W$.
key_observables: Dirac spectral density $ho(\lambda)$ near $\lambda 	o 0$, and the power-law exponent $p$ characterizing the DOS $ho(E) \propto E^p$.
important_parameters: Disorder strength $W$, lattice size $L$, and the energy $E$. The analysis focuses on the limits $W 	o \infty$ and $L 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the IR cutoff in the Anderson system should be viewed as descending from the randomness strength $W$, rather than the lattice size $L$, to correctly model the QCD IR sector.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the negative power-law behavior of the spectral density and the effective spatial dimension in the deep IR, comparing results for finite disorder strengths $W$ and showing extrapolations of the power-law exponent $p(W)$ towards $-1$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical connection between the QCD IR phase and scale-invariant spectral densities. It then applies this concept to the chiral Anderson model, analyzing the DOS behavior under increasing disorder strength $W$ and extrapolating the results to the thermodynamic limit to derive the universal exponent.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, solvable condensed matter model (chiral Anderson model) to test a deep theoretical prediction from high-energy physics (QCD IR phase), offering insights into how disorder can generate scale-invariant spectral features.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Structural fingerprints of the deep-IR (near λIR =0) Dirac structure for the system in IR phase. Left: negative power law behavior of spectral density. Right: effective spatial dimension of the modes. Note that dIR =3 for exact zero modes while dIR ≈2 for lowest near-zero modes.

Figure 2: Left: density of states for non-random spectrum (5) in D=3 over its spectral range (blue line) compared to the case of W =5 logarithmic noise. Right: zoom (log-log form) to the lowest part of the spectrum where DOS of L=16 random system doesn’t change upon increasing L.

Figure 3: Density of states for W =5, L=16 system in the lin-lin (left) and log-log (right) form over the entire spectral range. Effective spectral bounds ⟨Emin⟩and ⟨Emax⟩, as well as all explicit cutoffs are shown. See the discussion in the text.

Figure 4: Left: the average minimal positive eigenvalue as a function of 1/L for the system at W =5. The form of the fit was originally proposed in Ref. [6]. Right: the L-dependence of ρ(e−W/2) and ρ(e−W/4) at W =5. See the discussion in the text.

Figure 5: Spectral densities at W =5 in deep IR (E < e−W/2) with increasing L. Scales 1/L and ⟨Emin⟩are marked by vertical lines. Shaded bands delimit the regions 1σ, 2σ and 3σ away from ⟨Emin⟩(σ is the standard deviation). Lower right: the power p1 extracted from regions adjacent to ⟨Emin⟩+ 3σ, and shown by solid line segments, as a function of 1/L.
